findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the user has no topic_users record for the topic. This happens for a different logged-in user opening a forwarded link, or for a topic the user never interacted with. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle nil explicitly.

findings.title: State-changing GET toggles level on every visit and can be triggered by prefetchers
findings.body: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET that changes the notification level each time it is hit. The first visit from watching or tracking drops the user to regular; a reload or second click then drops them to muted. Email link scanners and prefetchers, which commonly fetch every link in a message, will silently change or mute users' subscriptions. The action should be idempotent (always set a fixed target level) or require an explicit confirmation POST.

findings.title: Direct save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: The level is updated with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) are not set and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published. If `notifications_reason_id` is still nil, `TopicUser.update_last_read` will auto-promote the topic back to tracking once the user's read time passes the threshold, silently undoing the unsubscribe. Open clients also show a stale notification state.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and MessageBuilder renders it for every email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`. Callers that do not pass `unsubscribe_url` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Examples are other mailers, plugins, or any non-topic emails that use this flag. The spec had to be changed to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which confirms the new requirement. Either make the per-topic sentence conditional or default the argument.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action has no controller specs. Untested behaviour includes the level transitions (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted), the slug redirect, the logged-out case, and the missing-TopicUser case. These are exactly the paths that currently misbehave.
